description:
## Why

Tier-2 corpus — pyca/cryptography's curated test corpus. Hundreds of weird, hand-picked certs targeting documented edge cases. Highest signal-to-noise of any external corpus.

## What

1. Shallow-clone pyca/cryptography to `~/GIT/cryptography` (per AGENTS.md source-of-truth rule). Identify the test corpus directory (likely `tests/x509/v1/` or similar; verify before coding the loader).
2. The PEM-tree corpus loader (PKIX-7nsf.4) should already handle most chain.pem files. Audit failures and extend loader if needed.
3. Run `pkix-difftest run pem-tree ~/GIT/cryptography/tests/x509/<...> --oracles pkix-path,openssl,pyca --output-md pkix-difftest/baseline-pyca.md --output-json pkix-difftest/baseline-pyca.json`.
4. Same hand-classification of divergences as PKIX-7nsf.6.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All discoverable chains in the pyca corpus produce a verdict from each oracle (or are explicitly filtered with a documented reason — e.g., 'this chain has only one cert and the harness requires ≥2').
- [ ] `baseline-pyca.md` and `baseline-pyca.json` committed.
- [ ] Every `LooserThanWild` entry has a follow-up bead or a written-out justification.
- [ ] At least one real divergence is found and recorded — this is the bead's project-level acceptance criterion ('at least one real divergence found, classified, and recorded').

## Notes

- pyca's corpus has lots of pem files that aren't full chains (single certs, key files, etc.). The loader needs a clear filter rule (e.g., 'only files matching glob ./certs/chain*.pem' or 'only directories containing chain.pem').
- This is where INTEROP.md (PKIX-7nsf.8) gets its first concrete examples.
